Commentary: Curtis Campher to Jack Brassell, 1 run, Brassell hangs back to the length delivery and tucks it in front of square on the leg-side and the batters scamper across
Curtis Campher to Ruben Trumpelmann, 1 run, back of a length on middle and leg, Trumpelmann works it to long leg

Curtis Campher to Jack Brassell, no run, brilliantly bowled! A back of a length delivery on off, pitches and seams in sharply. Brassell pushes at it but gets beaten on the inside-edge and the ball flies over the stumps
Curtis Campher to Jack Brassell, no run, hard length delivery on off, Brassell hangs back and punches it to covers
Curtis Campher to Jack Brassell, no run, full just outside off, Brassell drives it back to Campher who makes a half-stop to parry it towards mid-off
Liam McCarthy [5.0-0-33-0] is back into the attack
Liam McCarthy to Ruben Trumpelmann, 1 run, shortish delivery on off, Trumpelmann pulls it down to long leg and takes the single
Trumpelmann walks down the track to have a chat with Jack Brassell
Liam McCarthy to Jack Brassell, 1 run, short of length outside off, Brassell punches it to deep cover to bring Ruben Trumpelmann back on strike

Liam McCarthy to Ruben Trumpelmann, FOUR, crunched! A shortish delivery well outside off, Ruben Trumpelmann reaches out and flat-bats it powerfully past the right side of mid-off. The ball reaches the fence at the rate of knots

Liam McCarthy to Ruben Trumpelmann, FOUR, fifty for Trumpelmann! He has been quite superb. He has given a glimmer of hope to his side. He raises his bat and gets a good round of applause from his mates. Was a shortish delivery around off, sat up nicely for Trumpelmann. He stood tall and nailed the pull through mid-wicket to find the fence
Liam McCarthy to Ruben Trumpelmann, THATS OUT!! Bowled!!

Liam McCarthy to Ruben Trumpelmann, out Bowled!! That's the final nail in the coffin! McCarthy finishes things off with a beauty! In the corridor of uncertainty, pitches and straightens to open Trumpelmann up in his stance. He is rooted to the crease as he tries to keep it out but gets beaten on the outside edge. The ball hits the top of off. Ireland take a 1-0 lead in the 5-match series. Ruben Trumpelmann b Liam McCarthy 50(43) [4s-4 6s-3]

Gavin Hoey | Player of the Match: (On their brilliant outing) We're first of all delighted with the win to start off the series, and we hope to go on like that. (On his mindset during his spell) I wouldn't call it a consistent purchase, but there was definitely something in it for the spinners in the first innings so I was hopeful that if I got it in the right areas, that there would be something there for me. (On gaining good momentum from this game) Yeah, if the pitch plays similarly, I think we'll learn a lot from this game. Delighted to get a win on the first day.

Erasmus (2/2): Yeah, and then obviously with a new ball, I thought both teams sort of missed their mark and gave the opposition that powerplay start. So we want to clean that up, but those guys have been in phenomenal form. The batters have been in really good form in the top four, scoring big partnerships. Fortunately, today we didn't quite play that situation and that particular pitch very well. There was obviously a lot of variable bounce, but with a good outfield, I think there was still enough value for shots and for bad balls to get put to the boundary and the fielders to get put under pressure. Unfortunately, we just sort of allowed the leggie into the game, and then we were always under pressure against the rest of the guys. Trumpelmann showed the way to bat, maybe hitting a bit harder straight and putting some pressure back onto the bowler allows them to bowl outside those areas that sort of go up and down. So there's lots to learn for the next game, but we've been playing some good cricket.

Stirling (2/2): (On what stood out for him today apart from Gavin's bowling) Yeah, well, Gavin was top class. I think a lot of learning really stood out. I think we can get better in each facet. I think with the direct hits, we could hit a couple; there would have been an extra run out or two. I think we were a little bit loose with the new ball. We weren't accurate enough. I think in these conditions, it brings the sides closer together, and you've got to really be accurate, which isn't something that we speak about that often. It's actually been more about threatening and taking wickets and imposing ourselves, but actually here accuracy is really key, and I thought that's what Namibia showed really, really well. I think that was their strength. They didn't miss much. Their line and length was pretty darn good for most of the innings, and we found it tough, and actually they reaped their rewards in the last ten overs instead of possibly up front.

So, that's it from our side. Namibia's death bowling was superb and it looked like they will make a match of it. But, their inexperience with the bat at the highest level showed. They chanced their arms one too many times when the need of the hour was largely to milk the ball around. Ireland would be pleased especially with the fact that they defended 229 without breaking a sweat. Join us for the 2nd ODI from the Namibia Cricket Ground day after tomorrow. Until next time, goodbye and cheers!
